Small, practical help for questions, feedback, and trust details.
It helps more than you\'d think.
Quiet Grid works fully offline. No data leaves your device.
Quiet Grid does not collect, transmit, sell, or share personal data. The app does not require an account and does not send data to us or to third parties.
Quiet Grid stores a small amount of app data locally so the app can work as expected. This includes theme preference, local statistics, and active puzzle progress.
Quiet Grid does not use ads, analytics, tracking, crash reporting services, or third-party online services.
Quiet Grid is a privacy-first puzzle app built for calm focus.
Quiet Grid keeps logic puzzles lightweight, fully offline, ad-free, and free to use. The goal is simple: clear rules, supportive pacing, and no distractions.
Quiet Grid currently includes several puzzle games, with local statistics, dark and light themes, and no accounts.
Quiet Grid source code is available under the GNU General Public License v3.0.
Quiet Grid also uses open-source packages that keep their own licenses. You can review the full source code and package list in the project repository.

Word Guess\'s German word list is built from word-frequency data from the FrequencyWords project (hermitdave/FrequencyWords on GitHub), licensed CC BY-SA 3.0. English, Spanish, French, and Dutch word lists are built from Hunspell spelling dictionaries: LibreOffice\'s en_US dictionary (LGPL/BSD), RLA-ES\'s es_ES dictionary (LGPL), Dicollecte\'s French dictionary (MPL 2.0), and OpenTaal\'s Dutch dictionary (BSD/CC BY 3.0).
Quiet Grid is better because of the people who contribute to it. Thank you.
Want to see your name here?
Quiet Grid is open-source. Bug fixes, translations, and new puzzle ideas are all welcome — open a pull request on GitHub.

Each successful round adds one more number. Reach the maximum count to solve the puzzle.
Take a moment to trace a path through all numbers before tapping 1. A quick mental route is faster than searching mid-sequence.
Notice clusters of consecutive numbers. Tapping neighbours one after another is faster than jumping across the grid.
Score is based on total time across all rounds. Faster tapping earns a higher score.

Tap the first letter of a word, then tap the last letter to select. Words run in straight lines: horizontal, vertical, or diagonal.

Invalid word selections are silently ignored — no penalty for tracing wrong paths. Wrong hidden-word taps are different: once you\'re guessing the hidden word, a wrong tap resets your progress and costs accuracy.

Drag every piece from the tray onto the 8x8 grid. Clear full rows and columns to score points, and reach the target score to solve the puzzle.

Drag a piece from the tray below the board and drop it onto the grid. It can only be placed where every one of its cells lands on an empty square. Once all 3 tray pieces are placed, a new set of 3 appears.
There is no wrong move to undo — if none of your 3 current pieces can be placed anywhere on the board, the puzzle ends immediately.
Filling every cell in a row or column clears that entire line and scores points.
You always hold 3 pieces at once. A new batch only arrives once all 3 are placed, so think about where all three will fit before committing to the first.
Clearing more than one line at once, or clearing lines on consecutive placements, scores extra bonus points on top of the base line-clear score.
No valid moves ends the puzzle
If none of your 3 current pieces fit anywhere on the board, the puzzle ends. Keep the board from getting too fragmented.
Prefer clean lines over odd corners

Solid pieces (squares, rectangles, straight lines) clear predictably. Irregular shapes tend to leave small unusable gaps — place them early, while the board still has room to absorb the awkward leftover.
Save straight pieces for the finishing blow
Building the board up close to full, then dropping a long straight piece to clear it, is the most reliable way to bank a big score.

Placing a piece scores nothing on its own — only clearing a line scores points. Clearing multiple lines at once, or clearing on consecutive placements, adds further bonuses. Clearing the entire board scores the largest bonus. Solving the puzzle itself also earns a separate score based on how quickly you finish — starting at 50,000 and dropping over time.
